source_title: Boruto Revives The 2 Strongest Ninja Clans In History
source_excerpt:
Boruto: Two Blue Vortex is rapidly changing the scene in regard to the ninja villages and, with that, ninja clans as well. The vast majority of the series has been focused on the Otsutsuki Clan, but that doesn't mean the other clans that we know from the Naruto series have not been growing.
In the world of Naruto , the ninja world was dominated by many shinobi clans, and out of them, quite a few went extinct. In the Boruto era, a lot of these extinct clans are being revived, including two of the very strongest, those being the Uchiha and the Uzumaki. Boruto: Two Blue Vortex is especially expanding the Uzumaki Clan and, at the same time, adding multiple new members to clans like the Uchiha as well.
Boruto: Two Blue Vortex Is Bringing Back The Uzumaki Clan
The Uzumaki clan was a legendary clan that existed long ago in the Naruto world and had its own country in Uzushiogakure, also known as the Land of Whirlpools. The Uzumaki clan reigned supreme, but due to apprehension from neighboring countries, this village was eventually destroyed .
“My country no longer exists. Our Fuinjutsu were feared during the war, and eventually, our village was attacked and destroyed. The survivors apparently all scattered to various lands and went into hiding.” — Kushina Uzumaki explains the destruction of the Uzumaki Clan, Naruto Chapter #500
In the current world of Naruto and Boruto , the Uzumaki clan exists, primarily within Konoha. Right now, it is officially recognized as a separate clan of the village, unlike before. The current Uzumaki household is led by Naruto Uzumaki, the Seventh Hokage of Konoha. Alongside him are Hinata Uzumaki, who is a former member of the Hyuga clan, and their two children, Boruto Uzumaki and Himawari Uzumaki.
That said, the Uzumaki clan has now been expanded by the inclusion of Kawaki . In the Boruto series, Naruto Uzumaki adopted Kawaki into the Uzumaki household, and he now bears the name Uzumaki as well. In other words, the Uzumaki household has three next-generation characters who will carry the name and the legacy forward. When these characters grow up and eventually get married to have kids of their own, they will all expand the Uzumaki Clan even further. In a couple of centuries, the Uzumaki Clan will finally grow massively in numbers as well. The basis for all this is set in the Boruto: Two Blue Vortex series, and by the end of it, the Uzumaki Clan is going to be stronger than ever before.
“Kawaki sealed dad because he wanted to protect him. Besides, even if I free dad, it doesn't solve my problems with Kawaki.” — Boruto confirms Kawaki’s real goal, Boruto: Two Blue Vortex Chapter #6
Why The Uchiha Are Finally Back in Boruto
While the Uzumaki clan experiences a rapid expansion, the Uchiha are growing as well . Known to be one of the fiercest clans to ever live, the Uchiha were once the rivals of the Senju and played a significant role in the establishment of the village of Konoha. Unfortunately, before the Uchiha could grow further, Itachi wiped out the entire clan, leaving behind only Sasuke. With Obito, Itachi, and Madara officially dead, Sasuke was left as the last surviving member of the Uchiha Clan. However, after his marriage to Sakura, who also now bears the Uchiha name, the two gave birth to Sarada Uchiha. Currently, Sarada is the only heir of the Uchiha clan, but eventually she will go on to expand the clan in her own ways.
“You're all going to live here from now on, and I'm your father. My name is Kabuto! There's no need to be shy!” — Shin Uchiha clones are integrated into Konoha Orphanage, Naruto Spin-Off
More importantly, there are clones of Shin Uchiha, who was a specimen crafted by none other than Orochimaru , who have been taken in by the Konoha orphanage. All the Shin Uchiha clones have developed their own personalities, and in the near future, they will all add to the Uchiha Clan and serve different roles in the story. As such, through the Shin Uchiha clones, the Uchiha clan has already expanded significantly. As they grow older, they will most certainly integrate into Konoha and create a new Uchiha clan, restoring this clan to its former glory and adding new members to it as well.

The Uzumaki And Uchiha Dominate The Ninja World In Boruto
It is quite easy to see that the future of the Uchiha clan is quite bright in the Boruto series. Right now, the vast majority of the focus in Boruto goes to Sarada Uchiha, who, in the post-Momoshiki arc, is currently engaging in combat against Hidari. Boruto: Two Blue Vortex Chapter 39, which is set to be released on November 20, 2026, is going to see Sarada Uchiha grow even further in terms of strength. In the background, the other Shin Uchiha clones are also likely growing in power. Furthermore, Sasuke Uchiha's return is also on the horizon in the Boruto series, which means that after the post-Mamushi arc, the Uchiha clan will once again reach its peak.
Hidari: You could've collected their Thorn Soul Bulb if you wanted, so why didn't you? Or, rather, why did you bring me back?
Jura: Good question. I've never pondered the issue, but just now, when I tried to imagine a world without you in it, I experienced feelings of sadness.
— Ikemoto sets up Hidari's death, Boruto: Two Blue Vortex Chapter #35
By the end of the Boruto series, the Uchiha clan will be stronger than ever before, and given the power level of the Uzumaki, the two clans will be neck and neck. With the decline of the Senju, the Uchiha and the Uzumaki will stand tall as the two strongest clans in the entirety of Konoha and dominate the ninja world. Among the mortals, the Uchiha and the Uzumaki are going to be the strongest clans to exist. However, there is also the Otsutsuki clan to take into consideration.
Among the Otsutsuki, there are many powerful gods that have existed over the last millennia, and they will continue to exist as a monstrously powerful force in the ninja world. As such, the Otsutsuki will always remain at the top. In the world of the mortals, the Uchiha and the Uzumaki carry special importance, which will continue to be maintained for the next couple of centuries as well, long after the death of Naruto and Sasuke.
We are eagerly waiting to see how the Uchiha and the Uzumaki clans are going to be expanded upon following their revival in the Boruto era, and what ideas Mikio Ikemoto, the author of the Boruto series, has in store for them. For now, the vast majority of the focus is on Sarada Uchiha and Sasuke Uchiha, both of whom are going to play a significant role in the post-Mamushi arc, which will facilitate the fall of Hidari and the return of the leader of the Uchiha clan .
Boruto: Two Blue Vortex by Mikio Ikemoto, supervised by Masashi Kishimoto, is available for fans to read via Manga Plus and Viz Media .
